reasons: Claimed status is compliant and matches the playbook's preferred position for this rule, which is the absence of any non-solicit binding the Customer; nothing in the supplied paragraph (an Article 13 'MISCELLANEOUS' heading) or elsewhere in the cited material contains 'solicit', 'employ or engage', 'no-hire' or 'induce ... to leave' language.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline and no counterparty comment were proposed — the rendered redline is identical to the original text, so there is no over-flagging or invalid edit to correct.

The failed deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months, general-solicitation carve-out) are keyed to the fallback wording of an existing non-solicit; they are not probative where no non-solicit clause exists at all, so they do not undermine the finding.

Evidence is thin in that only an article heading is cited rather than affirmative clause text, but that is inherent to an absence-based compliant conclusion, and the rationale's note to resist any later-draft non-solicit beyond the fallback is accurate to the rule.
